text: In Kripke's theory, a sentence is called ___ if it has a truth value in the least fixed point, anchoring its truth-talk ultimately in non-semantic fact; the Liar lacks this property.
explanation: A sentence is grounded iff it receives a value in the least fixed point, meaning its truth is forced by the non-semantic facts. The Liar is ungrounded (valueless in every fixed point) and paradoxical; the Truthteller is ungrounded but merely underdetermined.
